paragraphs.text: Torwynn is a plane of scholars and magi who seek knowledge of spells across the Multiverse . Torwynn was created by Jeff Franzmann as the setting for his "Single Card Strategies" column. Single Card Strategies was initially published on Usenet, became a feature in The Duelist , and was later collected into a print volume.
Some place names on Torwynn are identical to place names on Dominaria . Each of those locations was named on a Magic card before its inclusion in Single Card Strategies.
Cameshbaan , a southern city noted for its bronze spires.
Blacksand , a coastal city at the mouth of the Evenfell River.
Catalion , a city in the northern mountains
Easthold , an island, possibly in the Wayfarer's Sea. The Lone Shell River Ghant , a southern city. Pasch , a northern city. Yarrow , a mountain city at the source of the Lone Shell River.
The Evenfell River , which runs from the falls near the Great Forest to a sea, possibly the Wayfarer's Sea.
The Institute for Arcane Study , distinct from the similarly-named institute on Dominaria .
The Lake of the Dead , distinct from the location of the same name on Dominaria.
The Mourning Lands , a marshy fen. Canticle's Tower , the observatory of Necromancer Emeritus Canticle.
The Sardian Mountains , distinct from the location of the same name on Dominaria. Barze , a city in the mountains.

The Vorthos Cast contrasted Torwynn with another plane, Antausia . The creator of Antausia, Shawn Carnes , was a member of the Creative team when he created that plane, but Franzmann was never a Wizards of the Coast employee. While acknowledging that Torwynn had been named in an official source ( The Duelist ), they reasoned that by virtue of the differing statuses of their authors, Antausia had been "inherited" into the canon, but Torwynn "hasn't exactly been inherited" in the same manner, and judged that neither plane would be revisited. Separately, one of the hosts of that podcast, Jay Annelli , opined that the plane is "semi-official".
The Fertile Lands of Saulvinia , depicting Antausia, was printed in 2023.
